solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Be on mobile phone with old person preferring old-style landline?

indicators.note: mobile = moving about, so the letters of PHONE with O move
in an across answer, BE 'on' the rest means it comes after it

parts.note: anagram fodder: PHONE with O (old) added
taken as it stands, placed last

explanation.surface: An elderly relative refuses a mobile and clings to the old landline on the hall table.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an example with a question mark: a neophobe fears anything new, and preferring the landline to a mobile is one case of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A neophobe is a person with a dread of novelty, so one who sticks to an old-style landline fits.

clue.text: Something groovy — a hit on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard, not seen, so we want a word that sounds like 'a hit'

parts.note: an arrow has a groove at its end to take the bowstring

explanation.surface: A catchy pop record gets airplay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groovy' is 1960s slang in the surface but literally means 'having a groove' here; with 'a hit on the radio' the clue pretends to be about a chart single.
explanation.definitionFit: A nock is the notch cut into an arrow for the bowstring, literally something with a groove.

clue.text: City workers' industrial action has no limits

indicators.note: limits are the ends, so both outer letters go

parts.note: a go-slow is a protest where staff work slowly on purpose
G and W removed from the ends

explanation.surface: A report of a strike that has spread without bounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' looks like the Square Mile of finance, suiting the workers in the surface, but it is simply the Norwegian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain example: the Norwegian capital is one city among many.

clue.text: One due to inherit fantastic wealth including a lot of land

indicators.note: fantastic = wildly unreal, so the letters of WEALTH are rearranged
the rearranged letters take in the next piece
a lot of, not all: the last letter is lost

parts.note: IRAN, a land, without its last letter

explanation.surface: An heir stands to come into a vast fortune with a big estate thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is so close to the answer's world that 'land' reads as acreage, but it is a country, Iran, cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir-at-law is the person entitled by law to inherit an estate.

clue.text: First sign of bitterness, say, with strong drink's flavouring

indicators.note: a word's first sign is the first thing you see of it, its opening letter

explanation.surface: A tasting note: the first bitter hint of a spirit's flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example' but is the verb, UTTER; the 's after 'drink' stands for 'is', leading to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterscotch is a flavouring of brown sugar and butter used in sweets and desserts.

clue.text: Nick mostly outside playing piece of music

indicators.note: most of the word, the last letter dropped
the shortened word goes around the next piece

parts.note: Old Nick is Satan; SATAN without its N
a show that is on is playing

explanation.surface: Nick, largely outdoors, is performing a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' is the Devil (Old Nick), not a person's name or a theft. S(ON)ATA.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonata is a musical composition, usually for one or two instruments.

clue.text: Mammal round mountains endlessly

indicators.note: the last letter is removed

parts.note: RANGE of mountains without its E

explanation.surface: An animal roams all around a mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: ORANG is short for orang-utan.
explanation.definitionFit: The orang, or orang-utan, is a great ape, a mammal.

clue.text: Like a diet of alien, with a pungent spice

indicators.note: alien = strange, so the letters of DIET OF are made strange

parts.note: the second 'a', taken as it stands

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an extraterrestrial's meals come with a strong seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram lands on FOETID, which is itself a fine description of this famously smelly spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Asafoetida is a strong-smelling resin spice used in Indian cooking.

clue.text: Teenager maybe soaring, having received financial help

indicators.note: the first word takes the second inside it

parts.note: an ascent is a rise; split A…SCENT
the dole is state unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: A teenager's spirits lift after getting a handout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' is there because most teenagers are adolescents but not every adolescent is a teenager. A(DOLE)SCENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An adolescent is a young person growing up, typically a teenager.

clue.text: Upright character enthralled by visits to nymph

indicators.note: held captive by, so the first piece sits inside the second

parts.note: one calls to see someone = visits; split CALL…STO
I is an upright stroke of a letter

explanation.surface: A straight-laced person is captivated by trips to see a nymph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright character' sounds like a moral person, but it is the letter I, which stands upright. CALL(I)S TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Callisto is a nymph of Greek myth, loved by Zeus and turned into a bear.

clue.text: Tried hard with slow movement, but one's dropped out

indicators.note: one is I, and it leaves the word

parts.note: an adagio is a slow piece of music

explanation.surface: Someone gave it their all, moving slowly, before one of them quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slow movement' reads as dragging feet but is a movement in music, the adagio.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a go is to attempt something, so 'had a go' means tried.

clue.text: Artist, male, one facing challenge rendered circle

indicators.note: rendered = made into something else, so CHALLENGE is rearranged

explanation.surface: A male artist is dared to draw a perfect circle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the story of Giotto drawing a perfect circle freehand; 'rendered' looks like an art word but rearranges the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Michelangelo was the Renaissance painter and sculptor of the Sistine Chapel ceiling.

clue.text: Drunken wager in hotel bar?

indicators.note: drunk = unsteady, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A tipsy bet is placed in a hotel bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags 'watering hole' as slang: animals drink at one, and so do people at the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A watering hole is jocular slang for a pub or bar where people go to drink.

clue.text: Put artist into mob to negotiate effectively

indicators.note: the first pieces go inside the next

parts.note: a horde is a mob; split HOR…DE
to set something down = to put it

explanation.surface: An instruction to plant a painter among a crowd to broker a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' reads as the instruction verb, but it supplies letters of its own; only 'into' gives the order.
explanation.definitionFit: To horse-trade is to bargain shrewdly, trading concessions to reach a deal.

clue.text: Left one quiet Berkshire town getting message silently

parts.note: Reading is a large town west of London

explanation.surface: Someone left a quiet Berkshire town and was sent word without a sound.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is pronounced 'redding' as a town, which hides the ordinary word 'reading'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip-reading is understanding speech by watching the mouth, taking in a message without hearing it.

clue.text: Old star, no good in Oxford college

indicators.note: G = good, and it is removed

parts.note: Rigel is a bright star in Orion

explanation.surface: A former celebrity is a failure at an Oxford college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old star' suggests a has-been celebrity, but O and the star Rigel are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A proper-name example: one of the constituent colleges of the University of Oxford, founded in 1326.

clue.text: Plan a chemist worked out for carbon capture

indicators.note: worked out = reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon, taken inside

explanation.surface: A chemist devises a carbon capture scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carbon capture' is a real climate technology, which makes 'capture' look like part of a noun phrase rather than an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A schematic is a diagram or plan showing how something is laid out.

clue.text: Little creature struggled to walk, beginning to meander off in distance

indicators.note: the shortened word goes inside the next

parts.note: a mile is a distance; split MIL…E

indicators.note: the first letter of 'meander', M, leaves the word

explanation.surface: A tiny creature hobbled off to wander into the distance.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that a millipede, with all those legs, is the last creature you'd expect to struggle to walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A millipede is a small many-legged arthropod.

clue.text: Walk round area with power to get vote

indicators.note: the first word goes around the next pieces

parts.note: a stroll is a walk; split STR…OLL

explanation.surface: A candidate canvasses a district with influence to win a ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like a joining word but is the abbreviation W.
explanation.definitionFit: A straw poll is an informal vote to gauge opinion.

clue.text: The Parisian fellow is deceived

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is taken in by a con.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow' means a college academic, a don, not just a man.
explanation.definitionFit: To be led on is to be misled or deceived into false hopes.

clue.text: A dear cat isn't to be disturbed in garden plant

indicators.note: disturbed = moved out of place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A beloved cat is not to be woken while it dozes among the flowerbeds.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is ironic: the letters are exactly what gets disturbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradescantia, or spiderwort, is a genus of garden and house plants.

clue.text: Old learner heard to get top grades?

indicators.note: we want what the pieces sound like, not how they are written

parts.note: EX = old (former), L = learner, said together

explanation.surface: A former student is said to have scored A grades.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner driver's plate in Britain. The question mark marks top grades as one example of excelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to do outstandingly well, as a student getting top grades does.

clue.text: Emperor, someone very funny cycling around

indicators.note: letters move from the front to the back, as on a wheel

parts.note: a hoot is a very funny person; HOOT with its first two letters moved to the back

explanation.surface: A comic ruler goes around on a bike.
explanation.walkthrough: Otho was Roman emperor for three months in AD 69, the year of the four emperors.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: he held the Roman throne briefly in AD 69 before taking his own life.

clue.text: Measure of certain fish caught and smuggled

parts.note: to run guns or drugs is to smuggle them

explanation.surface: Fish are netted and brought in illegally.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs to 'fish', so 'caught' is not a fishing word here; it is C, from cricket scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: A cran is an old measure of fresh herrings, about 750 fish.

clue.text: Each baked item has excellent crust

explanation.surface: Every pie on the counter has a superb pastry top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crust' is the pie's natural word, which hides that it is the instruction to wrap one piece around the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece means each, as in 'a pound apiece'.

clue.text: Three characters in succession 'arass traitor?

indicators.note: the dropped H in the clue's own spelling tells us to drop the H of the synonym

parts.note: three consecutive letters of the alphabet
harass = HECTOR, with the H dropped as in 'arass

explanation.surface: A Cockney accuses someone of treachery.
explanation.walkthrough: Any run of three letters could be meant; DEF is the one that fits. The question mark hedges: a defector crosses sides but need not betray anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A defector abandons their country or cause for another, which the other side calls treachery.

clue.text: Socialist sets on opponents at the table

parts.note: East and North are opposing partnerships at bridge

explanation.surface: A socialist attacks his rivals at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The table' is the bridge table, where E and N sit on opposite sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Engels co-wrote The Communist Manifesto with Marx.

clue.text: Funny show inadequate, now sadly a disappointment

indicators.note: sadly = badly, so the letters of NOW are rearranged
not enough of it, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: A reviewer finds a sitcom thin and a letdown.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a review whose verdict is the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedown is a letdown, a disappointing decline.
